sources.title: Core document forming part of the reports of States parties: Turkmenistan
sources.note: HRI/CORE/TKM/2009, dated 7 July 2010 and submitted 3 March 2009, page 10, paragraph 44: the Constitutional Act of 27 October 1991 proclaimed independence within the former Turkmen SSR borders.

sources.title: Permanent neutrality of Turkmenistan : resolution / adopted by the General Assembly
sources.note: A/RES/50/80 A, adopted without a vote at the 90th plenary meeting on 12 December 1995; PDF page 2 recognizes and supports permanent neutrality and calls on states to respect it.

sources.title: Library of Congress, Country Profile: Turkmenistan
sources.note: February 2007 profile, printed pages 1 to 3 and 11 to 12: page 1 independence; page 2 the 2002 attack and crackdown; page 3 hospital and rural-library closures, Niyazov’s death, and the early-February 2007 win; pages 11 to 12 the December 2006 death, ad hoc constitutional amendment, and election.

sources.title: United States Department of State, Background Notes: Turkmenistan
sources.note: January 2001 historical and government sections date independence, Niyazov rule, the 1994 referendum, and the December 1999 life presidency.

sources.title: Turkmenistan, Parliamentary Elections, 26 March 2023: ODIHR Election Assessment Mission Final Report
sources.note: Final report dated 9 October 2023; executive summary, PDF pages 3 to 5, and background and legal framework, PDF pages 5 to 7, cover institutions, restricted pluralism, media, results, and the 2023 reforms.

sources.title: Turkmenistan, Early Presidential Election, 12 March 2022: ODIHR Needs Assessment Mission Report
sources.note: Report dated 8 March 2022; PDF pages 3 to 7 document the pre-election handover call, Serdar Berdimuhamedow as a contestant, extensive presidential powers, limited pluralism, and the remote mission.

sources.title: Turkmenistan, Presidential Election, 12 February 2017: OSCE/ODIHR Election Assessment Mission Final Report
sources.note: Final report dated 10 May 2017; PDF pages 3 to 6 describe the controlled environment, missing genuine opposition, earlier election chronology, 2016 amendments, and seven-year presidential term.

sources.title: TÜRKMENISTANYŇ KONSTITUSIÝASY
sources.note: Official Turkmen text displayed 16 September 2016; article 21 names Turkmen as the state language and guarantees citizens the right to use their mother tongue.

sources.title: BMG-niň Hemişelik utgaşdyryjysynyň Adam hukuklary gününe bagyşlap eden çykyşy
sources.note: United Nations in Turkmenistan page dated 10 December 2025; the closing line supplies the exact Latin-script sentence “Adam hukuklary güni gutly bolsun!”

sources.title: The UN Resident Coordinator's message for Human rights day
sources.note: United Nations in Turkmenistan counterpart dated 10 December 2025; its closing line translates the sample as “Happy Human Rights Day!”

sources.title: Bilim hakynda (rejelenen görnüşi)
sources.note: Displayed Turkmen law title; article 5, clauses 1 to 8 cover Turkmen as principal instructional language, state-language teaching, mother-tongue support, and foreign-language study.

sources.title: Türkmenistanyň Halk Maslahaty hakynda
sources.note: Displayed title of the January 2023 Constitutional Law; especially articles 2 to 7 on the body, its membership, chair, and stated powers.

sources.title: World Bank, Turkmenistan Overview
sources.note: Country context and recent developments updated through 2024: hydrocarbons, state enterprises, labor, farming, water scarcity, soil quality, and transparency.

sources.title: UNDP Turkmenistan, Resilience, Climate and Energy
sources.note: Adaptation and water sections: rural livelihoods, women, livestock, agriculture water use, conveyance loss, Gokdepe pilot, urban waste, and climate education.

sources.title: Empowering local action against the climate change
sources.note: UNDP story dated 12 June 2019; the paragraph before “What has caused the change?”, that named section, its numbered results list, and the paragraph beginning “Over 100 farmers…” document gardens, dairy, local leadership, drainage work, water devices, land levelling, pumps, and consultations.

sources.title: Turkmenistan Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey 2015-2016: Final Report
sources.note: Cover dated January 2017; survey summary and tables WS.1 to WS.10, CP.6, and RH.6 cover households, water, sanitation, child feces, handwashing, marriage, and maternal care.

sources.title: Situation Analysis of Women and Children in Turkmenistan, 2024
sources.note: Pages 6 to 17 synthesize health access, vaccination, disability and education gaps, drinking water, sanitation, and agricultural water use.

sources.title: Turkmenistan Education Fact Sheets | 2021: Analyses for learning and equity using MICS data
sources.note: Figures 12 to 21 and 50 to 56 analyze foundational skills, regional and wealth gaps, attendance, computers, and internet access.

sources.title: UNICEF and Ministry of Education advance inclusive education in Turkmenistan
sources.note: November 2024 release: four pilot sites, School 74 assessment of sixteen students, multidisciplinary teams, and individualized education plans.

sources.title: Promoting Positive Parenting: Educators in Turkmenistan Completed Pilot Parenting Support Programme
sources.note: UNICEF release dated 26 November 2025: ten-week pilot in twenty-four preschools, twenty-four educators, about 250 parents, and practical home routines.

sources.title: Engaging parents in early learning
sources.note: UNICEF story dated 24 March 2019: weekly child-parent centres, home visits, caregiver demonstrations, and cooking and weaving activities for early learning.

sources.title: Heroes of #MyDream campaign organized by UNICEF Turkmenistan
sources.note: UNICEF photo essay dated 6 October 2020 records children describing ambitions including veterinarian, footballer, pilot, author, and pizzeria owner.

sources.title: Ministry of Health and UNICEF launched the Integrated Management of Childhood Illnesses program across Turkmenistan
sources.note: UNICEF release dated 4 March 2025: nationwide programme rollout, provider skills, health-system strengthening, and family and community practices.

sources.title: WHO Europe, Turkmenistan Country Day advances collaboration for EPW2
sources.note: 2 May 2025 page reports an 80 percent maternal-mortality reduction and nearly 45 percent under-five-mortality reduction since 2000.

sources.title: UNICEF, Mengli’s Story: The value of holistic care and early intervention
sources.note: May 2018 story follows a mother and child travelling six hours for multidisciplinary physical, speech, and family-centred early intervention.

sources.title: National Micronutrient Survey Among Women and Children in Turkmenistan
sources.note: Ashgabat, 2024, pages 3 to 15: 2,672 sampled households, women and children, diet and feeding, anemia, iodine, iron, folate, and vitamins A and D.

sources.title: Turkmenistan ensures sustainable investments in essential vaccines for all children
sources.note: UNICEF release dated 27 April 2017: partnership since 1994, government-financed procurement, HPV vaccination for girls and boys, and cold-chain support.

sources.title: UNICEF, Handwashing Sessions Go Live in Schools Across Turkmenistan
sources.note: October 2021 story: nationwide online school sessions, teacher videos, and glitter demonstrations on books, apples, cups, and other surfaces.

sources.title: UNICEF Launches New Country Programme for 2026–2030 to Advance Children’s Rights in Turkmenistan
sources.note: Page dated 29 January 2026 reports the 28 January launch; it gives 2021 to 2025 results for health workers, immunization, early childhood services, families, and schools, then sets priorities for the five-year programme.

sources.title: Traditional turkmen carpet making art in Turkmenistan
sources.note: Representative List 2019 description: wool, looms, five main tribal patterns, domestic and ceremonial uses, family transmission, and Carpet Day.

sources.title: UNESCO, Dutar making craftsmanship and traditional music performing art combined with singing
sources.note: Representative List 2021 description: two-string lute, mulberry body, apricot neck, craft process, musical genres, festivities, and gatherings.

sources.title: Art of Akhal-Teke horse breeding and traditions of horses’ decoration
sources.note: Representative List 2023 description: care, naming, contests, weddings, women-made decorations, young breeders, and formal and informal learning.

sources.title: UNESCO, Kushtdepdi rite of singing and dancing
sources.note: Representative List 2017 description: improvisation, gestures, good wishes, ceremonies, social cohesion, master-amateur transmission, schools, and cultural centres.

sources.title: UNESCO, Turkmen-style needlework art
sources.note: Representative List 2022 description: layered silk thread, looping method, regional motifs, everyday and ceremonial clothes, and mother-grandmother teaching.

sources.title: REGISTRATION CARD of the element of the Intangible Heritage of Turkmenistan in the National Inventory Form: Nowruz
sources.note: Translated Turkmen national-inventory registration card for the element Nowruz, section 1.4: three-day equinox celebration, semeni, cereal dishes, family and community events, children’s games, music, and dance.

sources.title: State Historical and Cultural Park “Ancient Merv”
sources.note: Brief synthesis and criteria: oasis cities, four millennia of settlement, Abbasid and Seljuk capitals, architecture, preservation, and 1999 inscription.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Parthian Fortresses of Nisa
sources.note: Brief description and criteria: Parthian centre, excavated domestic, state, and religious architecture, exchange routes, and 2007 inscription.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Kunya-Urgench
sources.note: Brief synthesis and criteria: eleventh-to-sixteenth-century monuments, sixty-metre minaret, architectural influence, conservation, and 2005 inscription.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Silk Roads: Zarafshan-Karakum Corridor
sources.note: Brief synthesis and criteria: 866-kilometre Tajikistan-Turkmenistan-Uzbekistan corridor, second century BCE to sixteenth century CE, and 2023 inscription.

proposedOverrides.name: Turkmenistan
proposedOverrides.summary: Modern sovereign Turkmenistan from the atlas’s approximate 1994 opening, with daily life, institutions, heritage, and an open continuing chronology.
